title: Add a one-time expense and see it in the cash flow
summary: Add a one-off cost, like a kitchen remodel, as an expense that starts and ends in the same year, then see it in Cash Flow.

chapters.label: Mark and Laura plan an $80,000 kitchen remodel in 2028.
Add it as an expense: choose Other and give it a name.
Enter the cost in today's dollars. Foundry adds inflation.
Set the start and end year to 2028, so it's paid once.
Select Add Expense to put it in the plan.
It's listed under Other Expenses, for 2028 only.
Open Cash Flow to see the effect year by year.
In 2028, spending jumps and net cash flow turns negative.
Drill into Expenses to see what's behind the jump.
The remodel shows up as Other, in 2028 only, grown with inflation.

steps: **Open Inflows & Outflows.** From a client's **Details**, choose **Inflows & Outflows**. The **Expenses** panel lists what the plan already spends.
**Add the expense.** In the **Expenses** panel, select **+ Add**. Set **Type** to **Other** and enter a **Name**.
**Enter the cost.** Type the amount in **Annual Amount ($)**. Leave **Amount in today's dollars** ticked to enter today's price and let Foundry add inflation.
**Make it one year.** For **Start Year** and **End Year**, choose **Manual** and enter the same year in both.
**Save it.** Select **Add Expense**. The expense appears under **Other Expenses**.
**Check the cash flow.** Open **Cash Flow** in the top bar. That year's expenses rise, and its net cash flow can turn negative.
**See what's behind it.** Select the **Expenses ▶** column header. The table breaks expenses down by category, and the cost shows in the **Other** column for that year only.
goodToKnow: An amount in today's dollars grows with inflation until its year, so Cash Flow shows more than you typed: $80,000 in 2028 appears as $83,886 at 2.4% inflation. Untick the box to enter the amount as it will be in that year.
The **Expenses** figure at the top of Inflows & Outflows covers the current year only, so a cost in a future year doesn't change it.
Cash Flow hides columns that are zero in every year. The **Other** column appears once the plan has an Other expense.
